s: to confuse, to throw off, to baffle, to perplex
to mistake, to confuse, to mix up (misidentify)
note: «Confundir A con B» = to mistake A for B. «Confundirse» = to make a mistake: «me confundí de calle» (I got the wrong street).
ex: A menudo me confunden con mi hermano.
I'm often mistaken for my brother.
Al principio, te confundí con tu hermano.
At first, I mistook you for your brother.

s: to agree, agree on, agree upon
to arrange (bring together various parts to build or form something)
note: Works like «gustar» for 'to suit': «te conviene descansar» (it's good for you to rest). «Convenir en» = to agree on. Conjugated like «venir».
ex: Convinimos en que lo haría yo, ¿no?
We agreed that I would do it, didn't we?
Conviene que te laves las manos antes de comer.
It's better if you wash your hands before you eat.

note: Means to practise a profession or wield power, not to exercise physically (that's «hacer ejercicio»): «ejercer la medicina», «ejercer presión».
ex: Todos deberían ejercer su derecho a voto.
Everyone should exercise their right to vote.
#51721 CK · #1965461 marcelostockle
Tu amigo ejerce una mala influencia sobre ti.
Your friend has a bad influence on you.
#2333726 AlanF_US · #4388814 pchamorro

s: to send off, dismiss (show someone a red card)
note: Used for expelling from school, a country or a game: «lo expulsaron del colegio»; in football, «expulsar» = to send off.
ex: Me acaban de expulsar del colegio.
I just got kicked out of school.
Expulsó a los estudiantes del salón.
He expelled the students from the room.

note: Transitive (to train someone) or intransitive/reflexive (to work out): «entreno/me entreno tres veces por semana».
ex: Ambos, Tom y Mary, entrenan a John.
Tom and Mary are both coaching John.
Me entreno dos horas al día.
I train two hours a day.
#9535711 DJ_Saidez · #1132670 Shishir

s: to suck, to stink, to blow
note: «Apestar a» = to stink of: «la cocina apesta a pescado». Figuratively, «esto apesta» = this stinks/sucks.
ex: El quitaesmalte apesta un montón.
Nail polish remover stinks a lot.
#469561 FeuDRenais · #1669153 teskmon
La habitación apestaba a tabaco.
The room stunk from the tobacco.
#13440515 rul · #359948 tatoerique

note: «Nadar en» = to be swimming in: «nadar en dinero» (to be rolling in money). «Nadar a braza/crol» for swimming strokes.
ex: A menudo voy a nadar al río.
I often go swimming in the river.
Algunos niños están nadando en el estanque.
Some children are swimming in the pond.

note: Means to exhibit or present (an idea, art), and to expose to risk: «exponerse al sol», «exponer una teoría». Conjugated like «poner».
ex: Un peatón imprudente se expone a sí mismo a un gran peligro.
A jaywalker exposes himself to great danger.
Exponga usted su idea con más claridad.
Explain your idea more clearly.
#2265923 _undertoad · #2265924 cueyayotl

note: To travel all over or cover a distance: «recorrimos Italia en tren», «recorrer diez kilómetros». Not 'to recur'.
ex: Este tren recorre entre Tokio y Hanata.
This train runs between Tokyo and Hakata.
#56474 CK · #1211589 marcelostockle
Este automóvil apenas recorrió 200 kilómetros.
This automobile only traveled 200 kilometers.
#8384095 cromwellt · #8379744 arh

note: Formal or police context: «la policía interrogó al sospechoso». For everyday questions use «preguntar».
ex: Él sabe cómo interrogar a las personas.
He knows how to interrogate people.
#1752054 Amastan · #1861500 marcelostockle
La policía quiere interrogar a Tom.
The police want to interrogate Tom.

note: Takes «a» or «con»: «contribuir a la paz», «contribuir con dinero». Spelling gains a y: «contribuyo, contribuyó».
ex: Todo el mundo puede contribuir.
Everyone is free to contribute.
#704150 jakov · #705735 Shishir
Cualquier cosa en la que eres bueno contribuye a la felicidad.
Anything you're good at contributes to happiness.

s: to save, to rescue, to deliver, to preserve
note: «Librarse de» = to get out of, escape: «me libré del examen». «Librar una batalla» = to wage a battle; in Spain «libro los lunes» = I have Mondays off.
ex: Tenemos que librarnos de todas estas cosas.
We need to get rid of all this stuff.
No es fácil librarse de los malos hábitos.
It's not easy to get rid of a bad habit.
#4150000 Eldad · #9706981 Shishir

s: to grit (e.g., one's teeth), to clench (e.g., one's fist)
to push down (e.g., a toilet plunger)
note: Stem-changing (aprieto). Also 'to be too tight': «estos zapatos me aprietan». «Apretar el botón» = to press the button.
ex: Tom se apretó el cinturón de seguridad.
Tom fastened his seatbelt.
El hombre se armó de valor y apretó el gatillo.
The man plucked up courage and pulled the trigger.
#1157726 Shishir · #1138742 Shishir

s: exclamation of rejection used to tell someone off
note: Vulgar. Common expressions: «cagarla» (to screw it up), «me cago en...» (strong curse), «cagarse de miedo» (to be scared stiff).
ex: Sospecho que alguien se cagó un pedo.
I suspect that someone farted.
#9097830 rafaeldejesus8199 · #9097825 rafaeldejesus8199
¿Estará Tom tratando de cagar nuestra noche?
Is Tom trying to ruin our evening?

s: to wound, injure (cause physical injury and pain)
to hurt, offend, wound (cause emotional pain)
to hurt oneself, to get hurt
note: Stem-changing (hiero, hirió). Physical or emotional: «herir los sentimientos de alguien». «Un herido» = an injured person.
ex: Hiere cuando los otros niños te ignoran.
It hurts when the other kids ignore you.
#681187 Source_VOA · #1610645 teskmon
A él le hirió una bala.
He was wounded by a bullet.

note: «Reflejarse en» = to be reflected in: «su cara se reflejaba en el agua». Also figurative: «el informe refleja la realidad».
ex: El agua refleja la luz.
Water reflects light.
El espejo refleja la luz.
A mirror reflects light.

s: to provide, to send, to deliver
note: Besides 'to make easier', in formal Spanish it means to provide: «le facilitaremos la información» (we'll provide you with the information).
ex: Estos libros facilitarán su trabajo.
These books will make your work easier.
#2268738 _undertoad · #2268739 Shishir
¿Es cierto que el jengibre facilita la circulación y mejora el metabolismo?
Is it true that ginger increases circulation and improves your metabolism?

s: to block (physically), to barricade, to obstruct
to jam, to wedge, to fix in place
to block, to impede, to hinder, to stymie
note: Also used for phones and social media: «bloquear a alguien en WhatsApp». «Bloquearse» = to freeze up, go blank.
ex: Un árbol caído bloqueaba el paso.
A fallen tree blocked the path.
Tom admitió que fue quien se dejó las ventanas sin bloquear.
Tom admitted he was the one who left the windows unlocked.

s: to back up, to go back, to step back, to move backward, to shrink back
to retreat, to fall back, to recede, to draw back
note: Intransitive: «retrocede un paso». «No hay que retroceder» = there's no turning back.
ex: El policía les pidió a las personas que retrocedieran.
The policeman asked people to back off.
#48470 CK · #1308684 marcelostockle
Es mejor retroceder que perderse.
It's better to walk back than to get lost.
#1287197 jakov · #1288118 marcelostockle

note: «Admirarse de» = to be amazed at. «Te admiro por tu valor» = I admire you for your courage.
ex: Todos los que le conocían le admiraban.
Everyone who knew him admired him.
No puedo evitar admirar su talento.
I can't help admiring his talent.

note: Always reflexive: «arrepentirse de» = to regret: «me arrepiento de no haber ido». Stem-changing (me arrepiento).

s: to catch (a ball, said especially of the goalkeeper)
note: Also colloquial 'to catch': «te cacé» (I caught you). «Cazar al vuelo» = to catch on quickly. Spelling: «cacé».
ex: Está prohibido cazar en los parques nacionales.
Hunting is banned in national parks.
#680336 Source_VOA · #962105 hundo
Él fue a cazar en el bosque.
He went hunting in the woods.
#299957 CK · #862235 jorgearestrepo

note: Formal synonym of «realizar/hacer»: «efectuar un pago», «efectuar una compra». Common in official or written Spanish.
ex: El mago efectúa varios trucos con cartas.
The magician performs a few card tricks.
#8946738 sundown · #12086127 Alejandr0
Se efectuó un censo en 2005.
A census was performed in 2005.
#4350974 AlanF_US · #4351088 umano

s: to kill (usually said as a joke)
to suicide (to kill someone and make their death appear to have been a suicide rather than a homicide)
note: Always reflexive: «suicidarse». Accent pattern: «se suicida». The noun is «el suicidio», the person «el/la suicida».
ex: El escritor se suicidó en su estudio.
The author killed himself in his study.
Ella se suicidó tirándose de un puente.
She committed suicide by jumping off the bridge.
#313262 Eldad · #574113 Shishir

s: to be caused by, to be due to, to be attributable to
note: Takes «a» with people: «obedecer a sus padres». «Obedecer a» also means to be due to: «el retraso obedece a la lluvia». Obedezco.
ex: Los niños deberían obedecer a la autoridad.
Children should obey authority.
#1655813 Spamster · #1663961 Shishir
Tenemos que obedecer las normas de tráfico.
We have to obey traffic rules.

note: Transitive: «derrotaron al campeón». The noun «la derrota» = defeat; «derrotado» also means exhausted or dejected.
ex: Desearía poder descifrar cómo derrotar al sistema.
I wish I could figure out how to beat the system.
#953724 CK · #1241406 marcelostockle
No puedes derrotar tú solo a Tom.
You can't defeat Tom alone.
#2208500 CK · #2828870 marcelostockle

note: Works like «gustar»: «me agrada la idea». Slightly more formal; «mucho gusto/encantado» are more common greetings.
ex: Los lloricas no le agradan a nadie.
Nobody likes crybabies.
#4056807 Lepotdeterre · #6607926 arh
Ese tipo de historia me agrada.
That kind of story appeals to me.
#2452029 sharptoothed · #10363321 DJ_Saidez

s: to mourn (often followed by la muerte de or la pérdida de)
note: «Lamento + subjunctive» is a polite 'I'm sorry that': «lamento que no puedas venir». «Lamentarse de» = to complain about.
ex: Dijo que lamentaba lo que había pasado.
He said he regretted what had happened.
#803346 Source_VOA · #803353 Shishir
Ella lamentó no haber seguido su consejo.
She regretted that she had not followed his advice.

note: Usually «basarse en» = to be based on: «la película se basa en un hecho real». «Basado en» = based on.
ex: Lo digo basándome en mi propia experiencia.
I say this from my own experience.
#58998 bluepie88 · #922703 Shishir
¿En qué se basa el argumento?
What is the basis for the argument?

note: Common for food, energy and drugs: «consumir alcohol». «Consumirse» = to waste away; «consumirse de celos» = to be eaten up with jealousy.
ex: Él fue apartado del equipo por consumir drogas.
He was dropped from the team for using drugs.
#303841 CK · #339674 tatoerique
Las selvas tropicales producen oxígeno y consumen dióxido de carbono.
Tropical rainforests produce oxygen and consume carbon dioxide.
#282138 papabear · #1731139 Shishir

s: to reclaim, to recover possession of
to claim, to ask for, to demand
to lure (with a decoy or whistle while hunting)
to look for (a criminal), to summon (a witness)
to protest, to complain, to object, to clamor, to reclaim
note: False friend: mostly 'to complain/demand', not 'reclaim': «reclamar al seguro», «reclamar una devolución». «Reclamación» = complaint.
ex: Reclamaré lo que me pertenece.
I'll take what's mine.
Los objetos que no se reclamaron se vendieron en la subasta.
The unclaimed items were sold off at auction.
#752991 darinmex · #755834 Shishir

note: Conjugated like «decir» except the future/conditional (bendeciré) and participle «bendecido». «Bendito» is the adjective: «¡bendito sea!».
ex: Dios bendice a los que se arrepienten.
God blesses those who repent.
#1343963 Chrikaru · #1345692 Shishir
Asimismo, yo te bendigo este día.
I likewise bless you this day.
#1167328 rul · #1167580 marcelostockle

note: Impersonal, stem-changing: «llueve». «Llover a cántaros» = to pour. «Llueve sobre mojado» = when it rains it pours.
ex: Acabábamos de empezar cuando comenzó a llover.
We had hardly started when it began to rain.
Apenas había salido cuando empezó a llover.
I had hardly left home when it began raining.

note: «Contentarse con» = to be satisfied/make do with: «me contento con poco».
ex: Algunas personas se contentan con poco.
Some people don't need a lot to be happy.
#10367235 DJ_Saidez · #1576663 Shishir
El hombre solitario se contenta con observar a las hormigas.
The lonely man derives pleasure from observing ants.
#48147 Lumi · #1510046 marcelostockle

s: to swallow (to cause to pass from the mouth into the stomach)
to swallow, consume, absorb (take (something) in so that it disappears)
to gulp, swallow, devour (eat quickly and eagerly)
to buy into, fall for (easily believe something without questioning)
note: Colloquial «no lo trago» = I can't stand him. «Tragarse» = to swallow (also to believe a lie): «se tragó el cuento».
ex: Me duele la garganta al tragar.
My throat hurts when I swallow.
No puedo tragar estas pastillas sin un vaso de agua.
I can't swallow these tablets without a drink of water.

s: to gather together, socialize, get together, come together, consort
transitive, colloquial, El Salvador, Costa Rica, Uruguay
note: «Juntarse con» = to hang out with or get together: «se junta con malas compañías». «Juntar dinero» = to save up money.
ex: Nos juntamos a la puerta de casa.
We met at the door of my house.
#2270017 _undertoad · #2270018 cueyayotl
"Una piedra rodante no junta musgo" es un refrán.
"A rolling stone gathers no moss" is a proverb.
#1503 CK · #180517 cueyayotl

s: to join a group, institution, organization, etc.
note: «Ingresar en/a» = to join or be admitted: «ingresar en la universidad», «lo ingresaron en el hospital». Also to deposit money.
reg: Spain: «ingresar dinero» is the usual way to say to deposit money. LatAm: «ingresar a» is preferred over «en» for entering an institution.
ex: No es necesario ingresarlo en el hospital.
It's not necessary to put him in the hospital.
#1037208 GPHemsley · #340001 tatoerique
La ingresaron en el hospital.
They admitted her to the hospital.
#680086 Source_VOA · #803387 Shishir

s: to toast, drink (a toast) to (to engage in a salutation and/or accompanying raising of glasses while drinking alcohol in honor of someone or something
to offer, provide, bring (to give what is needed or desired)
to yield (to produce as a return)
to dedicate (to designate (a bull) as being for another person as a mark of respect or affection)
to offer (to propose or express one's willingness (to do something))
note: «Brindar por» = to toast: «brindemos por los novios». In formal register it means to offer: «brindar apoyo», «brindar una oportunidad».
ex: ¡Brindemos por una larga y dichosa vida!
Here's to a long and happy life!
Ella les brindó una cálida bienvenida.
She extended a warm welcome to them.

note: «Rescatar a alguien de algo» = to rescue someone from something. Note the «a» before people.
ex: Ella hizo todo lo que pudo para rescatarlo.
She did her best to rescue him.
Los bomberos les rescataron del ascensor.
The firefighters rescued them from the elevator.
#7633641 kaesekaiser · #5721195 arh

s: to calm, to calm down, to tranquilize
note: «Tranquilízate» = calm down. Spelling: «tranquilicé». Often used to reassure: «me tranquiliza saberlo».
ex: Tranquilízate. Iré tan pronto como sea posible.
Calm down. I'll come over as soon as possible.
#325193 CK · #1305433 marcelostockle
Ella se tranquilizó antes de hablar.
She composed herself before speaking.
#317523 CM · #873446 jorgearestrepo

s: to cede, to hand over, to convey
to relinquish, to abandon, to leave, to give in
to decrease, to lessen, to diminish
note: «Ceder el paso» = to give way/yield (traffic). «Ceder a la presión» = to give in to pressure. «Ceder el asiento» = to give up one's seat.
ex: El puente cederá ante una carga tan pesada.
The bridge will give way under such a heavy load.
La tierra cedió bajo sus pies.
The earth gave out under his feet.

note: Conjugated like «tener» (retengo, retuve). Used for detaining people, withholding pay, and retaining information.
ex: A Sami lo estaban reteniendo contra su voluntad.
Sami was being held against his will.
#7190265 OsoHombre · #13466227 Seael

note: Formal 'to perceive', and also to receive a salary: «percibir un sueldo». Everyday alternatives: «notar», «darse cuenta de».
ex: Cuando llegué a casa, percibí que había perdido mi billetera.
When I got home, I noticed that I had lost my wallet.
No siempre puede percibirse a simple vista.
It cannot always be perceived by the naked eye.
#1020597 CM · #1434299 marcelostockle

note: «Ofenderse por» = to take offence at: «se ofendió por el comentario». «No te ofendas» = no offence.
ex: No te ofendas.Tom se comporta así con todos.
Don't be offended. Tom's that way with everyone.
Mi intención no era ofenderte.
I didn't mean to hurt you.
#17044 CK · #1868854 wallebot

s: to trace, to retrace, to trail, to backtrack, to scour
note: To track or trace: «rastrear un paquete», «rastrear una llamada». The noun «el rastro» = trace/trail.
ex: Él rastreó a su gato perdido todo el día.
He hunted for his missing cat all day.
Debemos volvernos a la edad media para rastrear su origen.
To determine its origin, we must go back to the middle ages.
#1008944 AOCinJAPAN · #1294003 marcelostockle

note: «Inclinarse por» = to lean toward/prefer: «me inclino por la primera opción». «Inclinar la cabeza» = to bow one's head.
ex: Esta casa se inclina hacia un lado.
This house is leaning to one side.
Los estudiantes se inclinaron ante su maestro.
The students bowed to their teacher.
#271867 CK · #4986544 cueyayotl

note: «Brillar por su ausencia» = to be conspicuous by one's absence. The noun «el brillo» = shine; «brillante» = brilliant.
ex: Una luz roja brillaba en la oscuridad.
A red light was glowing in the dark.
Las estrellas brillaban en el cielo.
The stars shone in the sky.
#1079126 keira_n · #5549076 Shishir

s: to tie, tie up, tie down, to tether (secure (something) by rope or the like)
to constrain, limit (prevent or remove movement, leave (someone or something) without freedom of movement or ability to act)
note: «Atar cabos» = to put two and two together. «Estar atado de pies y manos» = to have one's hands tied.
reg: LatAm: «amarrar» is very common for tying things (and shoes); «atar» is more typical in Spain.
ex: Ella le ayudó a atarse la corbata.
She helped him tie his tie.
¿Me podrías ayudar a atarme los cordones?
Could you help me tie my shoes?

note: «Completar un formulario» = to fill out a form. The adjective «completo» also means full: «el hotel está completo».
ex: Necesitó más tiempo para completar la tarea.
He needed more time to complete the task.
Complete con su nombre y dirección.
Fill in your name and address.

note: To call or summon: «convocar una reunión», «convocar una huelga». «La convocatoria» = the call (for applications, a meeting, a team).
Transitive or intransitive: «disminuir la velocidad», «el paro disminuyó». Spelling gains a y: «disminuye».
ex: La biodiversidad continúa disminuyendo cada año.
Biodiversity continues to decline each year.
#430072 witbrock · #1890548 teskmon
La calidad del arroz está disminuyendo.
The quality of rice is going down.

s: to burn, blaze (to be consumed by fire or in flames)
to burn, to sting, to smart (to hurt, be in pain)
to burn, seethe (to be in an agitated or angry mental state)
to rot (to suffer decomposition due to biological action)
to cause someone resentment or irritation
intransitive, chiefly  in the third person, colloquial, Mexi
note: Also to sting: «me arden los ojos». «Arder en deseos de» = to be dying to. «La cosa está que arde» = things are heated.
ex: Descubrí que su casa estaba ardiendo.
I found that his house was on fire.
Ardo en deseos de escuchar lo que opina usted sobre este asunto.
I look forward to hearing your thoughts on this matter.

s: to replace, to take the place of
note: «Sustituir A por B» = to replace A with B: «sustituí el azúcar por miel». Spelling gains a y: «sustituyo».
ex: Sustituí a mi padre en el negocio.
I took over the business from my father.
#566063 sacredceltic · #1604988 teskmon
El azúcar sustituyó a la miel como endulzante.
Sugar replaced honey as a sweetener.
#21001 lilygilder · #1625424 marcelostockle

note: «Consultar algo con alguien» = to consult someone about something. «Consultar el diccionario» = to look it up in the dictionary.
ex: Deberías consultar con tu abogado sobre este asunto.
You should confer with your attorney on this matter.
Deberías consultar con tu médico.
You should consult your doctor.
#28066 CK · #9859308 hayastan

note: Also colloquially to reckon/estimate: «calculo que llegaremos a las diez».
ex: Vamos a calcular los gastos del viaje.
Let's figure out the cost of the trip.
#2259030 _undertoad · #2259031 cueyayotl
Calculó que le costaría 100 dólares.
He calculated that it would cost him 100 dollars.

note: «Limitar con» = to border: «España limita con Francia». «Limitarse a» = to restrict oneself to: «se limitó a sonreír».
ex: Mi madre se limitó a llorar.
My mother did nothing but weep.
Por favor limita tu presentación a 30 minutos.
Please limit your presentation to 30 minutes.

note: «Reemplazar A por/con B» = to replace A with B. Near-synonym of «sustituir». Spelling: «reemplacé».
ex: Ella reemplazó la margarina por manteca.
She substituted margarine for butter.
#309926 CK · #962826 hayastan
Necesito reemplazar mi piano por uno nuevo.
I need to replace my keyboard with a new one.
#679882 ulyssemc1 · #1527999 marcelostockle

s: to ditch; to dump; to break up with
note: To kick: «patear el balón». Also colloquially to walk a lot: «patear la ciudad».
reg: LatAm: «patear» is the everyday verb for kicking. Spain: «dar una patada/dar patadas» is more usual; «patearse» there means to walk all over a place.
ex: Patea lo más fuerte que puedas.
Kick as hard as you can.
Patee lo más fuerte que pueda.
Please kick as hard as you can.
#4953776 Aria · #4952810 cueyayotl

note: Neutral/formal 'to change or alter': «modificar un documento». Spelling: «modifiqué».
ex: El Gobierno tuvo que modificar su política exterior.
The government had to alter its foreign policy.
Insistí de que modificáramos nuestro plan original.
I insisted that we change our original plan.
#252225 CK · #1750241 marcelostockle

note: Formal 'to raise': «elevar el nivel», «elevar una queja». In maths, «elevar al cuadrado» = to square.
ex: Una grúa eleva materiales de construcción pesados.
A crane raises heavy construction materials.
#681840 Source_VOA · #1306678 Shishir
Empezó a elevar la voz a medida que hablaba.
Her voice began to rise as she spoke.

note: «Comparar A con B»: «no me compares con él». «No tiene comparación» = it's incomparable.
ex: A menudo me comparan con mis hermanos.
I'm often compared to my brothers.
#837549 sacredceltic · #1337863 Shishir
Compara ambos atentamente y verás la diferencia.
Compare the two carefully, and you will see the difference.

note: Mostly reflexive: «enojarse con alguien» = to get angry at someone; «enojarse por algo» = about something.
reg: LatAm: «enojarse» is the everyday word for getting angry. Spain: «enfadarse» is the normal word; «enojarse» sounds literary or strong.
ex: Estoy seguro de que mamá se enojará.
I'm sure Mom will get mad.
#63375 Dejo · #866025 jorgearestrepo
No hay necesidad de enojarse tanto.
There's no need to get so angry.
#41525 CK · #6614478 UsuarioX

note: «Reaccionar ante/a» = to react to: «reaccionó mal ante la noticia».
ex: Veamos cómo reacciona Tom a eso.
Let's see how Tom reacts to that.
Sabía cómo iba a reaccionar.
I knew how you'd react.

note: Stem-changing (ruedo). Also to film a movie: «rodar una película»; «el rodaje» = the shoot.
ex: La pelota rodó hasta el arroyo.
The ball rolled into the stream.
#19553 papabear · #1534637 marcelostockle
La pelota rodó por el pasto.
